a11y.adjust-shape-styles.meaning: Name of a row in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog's Accessibility group, shown beside the key combination Cmd/Ctrl+Enter. It describes what that key does: it moves keyboard focus to the style panel so the user can change the selected shape's styles (color, fill, size and so on). 'Adjust' is a verb; 'styles' means the shape's appearance properties. The row is display-only and has a no-op handler.
constraints: Shortcut dialog row label; keep short
Describes a keyboard shortcut for keyboard and screen-reader users

a11y.enlarge-shape.meaning: Label of the 'enlarge-shapes' action, which scales the selected shapes up. Its handler resizes each selected shape about the selection center. It appears as a row in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog's Accessibility group. It is a verb phrase meaning to make bigger, not to zoom the camera. The English is singular, but the action applies to every selected shape.
constraints: Shortcut dialog row and action label; keep short
Pairs with 'Shrink shape' (a11y.shrink-shape); keep the two clearly opposite

a11y.enter-leave-container.meaning: Name of a row in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog's Accessibility group, shown beside Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down. It describes keyboard navigation: with a frame or group selected, the keys move selection into it (enter) or back out to its parent (leave). 'Container' means a frame or group shape that holds other shapes, not a UI panel or a software container. The row is display-only.
constraints: Shortcut dialog row label; keep short
'Enter' is the verb 'go into', not the Enter key

a11y.move-shape.meaning: Name of a row in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog's Accessibility group, shown beside the arrow keys. It describes what the arrow keys do: they nudge the selected shape in that direction on the canvas. 'Move' is a verb and 'shape' is a canvas object. The row is display-only.
constraints: Shortcut dialog row label; keep short

a11y.move-shape-faster.meaning: Name of a row in the Keyboard shortcuts dialog's Accessibility group, shown beside Shift plus the arrow keys. It describes what that combination does: it nudges the selected shape by a larger step than the plain arrow keys. 'Faster' means bigger steps per key press. The row is display-only. It pairs with 'Move shape'.
constraints: Shortcut dialog row label; keep short
